BiblicalUsage: Beth-Gilgal means house of the wheel, and it appears once, in Nehemiah 12:29, where the singers gathered from the villages around Jerusalem — from Beth-gilgal among them — for the dedication of the wall. The name never stands as a single word in the Hebrew text; it comes as two words, house and Gilgal, joined together.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe it is a small, glad note in Nehemiah's story: singers coming in from the villages to fill the city with praise.
